articleTitle: Efficient Space-Ground Federated Learning Based on Compressed Sensing
abstract: Satellite communication (SatCom) networks based on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites play an important role in the sixth-generation mobile communication network (6G) and Terrestrial-Aerial-Space network. However, traditional SatCom faces the following challenges: 1) The lack of computing power of satellite nodes. 2) Limitations of communication bandwidth. 3) The risk of node data being leaked. To tackle the challenges, in this paper, we propose an efficient space-ground federated learning (FL) algorithm based on compressed sensing (CS). The proposed framework improves upon the existing frameworks by allowing terminal nodes to send quantized data to the central server after compression with a random measurement matrix. Based on that, the central server updates the global model parameters utilizing the result of sparse reconstruction obtain by Bilinear Adaptive Generalized Vector Approximate Message Passing (BAd-GVAMP). Experiments on both independent and identically distributed (IID) datasets and non-IID datasets show that the proposed framework is able to reach high training accuracy while achieving substantial compression of model parameters and communication delay. The proposed framework enables high-efficiency and high-precision space-ground FL by fully utilizing the computing power of terminal nodes, tackling the communication bottleneck problem of SatCom, and protecting node data from leakage.

articleTitle: Design of Low Earth Orbit Satellite-Based Switch System
abstract: The satellite internet is the primary focus of the space economy, with low-earth orbit satellites being the trend in its development. Onboard satellite switches are responsible for facilitating data transmission between satellites and ground stations, as well as between satellites themselves, making them a crucial component in the design of low-earth orbit satellites. This paper aims to elucidate the issues and challenges faced in the design of onboard satellite switches for low-earth orbit satellites, and proposes an implementation scheme for these switches. It provides detailed insights into the design and concepts of the key components, and concludes with an analysis of the impending challenges in the development of low-earth orbit satellites, calling for collaborative efforts among researchers in satellite communication and offering insights to the research community.

articleTitle: Data Balancing in SAT-NET: Effects on Logistic Regression and Random Forest Performance
abstract: In the context of Satellite Internet Services and Applications (SAT-NET), data imbalance presents a significant challenge, severely impacting the performance of classification algorithms. This study investigates the impact of data balancing techniques, particularly the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), on the classification accuracy of logistic regression and random forest algorithms. Experimental results reveal that while SMOTE significantly reduces the accuracy of the logistic regression algorithm, it has minimal impact on the random forest algorithm, which maintains stable performance on both balanced and imbalanced datasets. This research provides empirical insights into the role of data balancing techniques in different classification algorithms and offers valuable guidance for algorithm selection and data balancing methods in SAT-NET data processing. Future research directions include exploring combinations of various data balancing techniques and their effects in different SAT-NET application scenarios to further enhance classifier performance. Keywords- Satellite Internet data imbalance; SMOTE; logistic regression; random forest; classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Priority Sketch: A Priority-aware Measurement Framework
abstract: Network measurement plays a crucial role in modern communication systems, including satellite networks and data centers. Sketches, a series of probabilistic data streaming algorithms, have been widely used in network measurement due to their efficiency and scalability. However, ensuring the Quality of Services (QoS) for high-priority traffic requires more precise measurement techniques. Despite their widespread use, existing sketches lack the capability to differentiate between priority levels, which is essential for priority-aware measurement. In this paper, we propose Priority sketch, a framework that can make many existing sketches priority-aware. We devise an attention function to adjust the accuracy for different priority levels, and optimize the accuracy by trimming counters. Extensive experiments show that the Priority sketch is $10 \times$ more accurate than the baseline solution.

articleTitle: Research on Group handover strategy of low-orbit satellite users
abstract: Due to the high mobility of satellites and their limited coverage areas, multiple users in close proximity may simultaneously need to switch to another satellite to maintain stable communication as the current satellite moves out of range. This simultaneous switching can lead to a surge in user handover requests when the satellite is about to exit the coverage area, causing a sharp increase in the processing load of the target satellite. The core network’s limited processing capacity exacerbates this issue, making it difficult to handle a large number of handover requests within a short time. To alleviate the congestion caused by this surge in handover requests, this paper proposes a clustering algorithm for LEO (Low Earth Orbit) satellite user terminals based on adaptive spectrum clustering. Users are clustered according to their spatial location, target handover satellite, and other relevant attributes. These clusters are then managed by a group head that initiates a unified handover on behalf of all users in the group, effectively reducing system signaling overhead and improving the success rate of large-scale concurrent handovers.

articleTitle: Failure Models for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks
abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), which integrate the satellite network, aerial network and terrestrial network, have been widely envisioned as a promising network architecture for satellite internet. However, SAGINs are facing more and more threats from both natural disasters and human attacks, causing various network failures. This paper presents a review on failure models for SAGINs, which are crucial for network vulnerability assessment due to network failures. By classifying the network failures into three basic categories (i.e., link failures, node failures and region failures), we first present the corresponding three basic failure models for SAGINs, and then introduce the more general failure models in SAGINs based on different combinations of these basic failure models. Finally, some open issues of failure modeling in SAGINs are discussed.

articleTitle: The Utility Optimization of Type I-PTT for Satellite Internet Navigation Location Information Protection
abstract: With the realization of direct-to-handset in Huawei smart phones, satellite communication has become a part of daily life, raising more and more concerns on security. Local differential privacy is a promising method for safeguarding user data in satellite communication, such as navigation positioning service system. With the purpose of protecting location data in navigation positioning services, this study focuses on the utility optimization of type I-PTT, optimizing the worst-case variance while ensuring completeness and unbiased estimation. Compared to the Duchi mechanism, we can conclude that at lower levels of privacy, the utility of I-PTT is lower than that of the Duchi mechanism and vice versa. These findings have significant implications for enhancing satellite internet privacy.

articleTitle: Multi-Access Resource Scheduling for Data and Relay Satellitess Based on a Genetic-Ant Colony Hybrid Algorithm
abstract: The resource scheduling of Data and Relay Satellites plays a fundamental role in enhancing system performance, and increasing user satisfaction. This paper focuses on the scheduling of S-band multi-access link resources of Data and Relay Satellites. The objective is to maximize the completion of high-priority tasks and minimize the overall scheduling time. Drawing inspiration from the operational strategies of workshop scheduling models, a multi-objective scheduling model with time windows is constructed. Due to the high-dimensional mixed integer optimization nature of this problem, obtaining the global optimal solution is challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes a geneticant colony hybrid scheduling algorithm for multi-access resource scheduling. Simulation results demonstrate that, under the same task conditions, the genetic-ant colony hybrid algorithm improves scheduling performance by 8.78% and 5.38% compared to the single genetic algorithm and the single ant colony algorithm, respectively. Furthermore, it reduces scheduling processing time by 16.21% and 29.36%, respectively.

articleTitle: A DRL-Based Dynamic Resource Allocation and Task Offloading Algorithm for LEO Satellite Network
abstract: With the rapid development of the low earth orbit (LEO) satellite network and Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) technology, researchers have found that by deploying MEC servers in LEO satellites, computation offloading services can be provided for remote areas where there is a lack of terrestrial MEC servers. As the number of ground users increases, the complexity of LEO satellite computation offloading scenarios has grown significantly. However, existing studies have difficulties dealing with scenarios characterized by high arrival rates and complex tasks. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-Based Dynamic Resource Allocation and Task Offloading (DDRATO) algorithm. We model the computation offloading problem in LEO satellite MEC networks with the optimization objective of minimizing the average offloading delay. We consider the impact of Amdahl’s law on computational performance and allocate the MEC servers’ computing resources to enable multitask parallel processing. Additionally, we transform the model into a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and solve it using the Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) algorithm. The experimental results show that the DDRATO algorithm significantly reduces the average processing delay in complex computation offloading scenarios, thus effectively compensating for the performance deficiencies in other algorithms.

articleTitle: SUNET: Framework, Security, and Privacy
abstract: SUNet (Satellite-assisted Unmanned-system Network) integrates satellite communication technology, unmanned equipment systems, and ground support facilities. Compared to traditional network system, SUNet has the advantages of flexible deployment and wide communication range. SUNet with cloud services (SUNET) breaks the limitation of satellites processing large-scale data, and integrates a large scope of computing and storage resources in a system. However, SUNET also poses more serious security risks than traditional networks for two reasons: i) the unique network framework, such as highly dynamic topology, unfixed network access points and decentralized control, of SUNET increases security risks, and ii) the rising probability of existing neighbor nodes with quantum computing. This paper firstly introduces the term SUNET from definition and compares SUNET with several related network frameworks. Then we anaylze the security risks, such as untrust between nodes, unauthorized access and quantum computing attack, faced by SUNET. Meanwhile, we illustrate the security requirements and the corresponding solutions, such as authentication, fine-grained authorization and quantum security, in SUNET. Finally, we discuss the security countermeasures and point out the potential future research directions.

articleTitle: GNSS Signal Spoofing Detection based on Satellite Oscillator Stability
abstract: Global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) provide all-weather timing, positioning and navigation services, playing a crucial role in both military and civilian applications. Despite their widespread use, GNSS is vulnerable to severe signal spoofing attacks. In this paper, we propose a novel GNSS signal spoofing detection method by exploiting the radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) of GNSS satellites. We introduce a new RFF feature named satellite oscillator stability, which is closely related to the hardware impairments of GNSS satellites and extracted from the GNSS receiver carrier tracking loop. Utilizing this new feature, we propose a GNSS signal spoofing detection method, which takes the extracted satellite oscillator features as input and employs a Residual Network as a classifier to distinguish between legitimate and spoofed signals. For verification, we use the most widely used GPS and Beidou signals, and conducted experiments in two scenarios: GPS generative spoofing and Beidou forwarding spoofing. The experimental results demonstrated that our proposed method achieve a detection accuracy of over 98% in the GPS generative spoofing scenario, and over 93% in the Beidou forwarding spoofing scenario.

articleTitle: Covert Communication in Satellite-Terrestrial Systems with a Full-Duplex Receiver
abstract: This paper investigates the covert communication in a satellite-terrestrial system, including a satellite transmitter Alice, a terrestrial full-duplex receiver Bob and a terrestrial warden Willie. To help the covert transmission from Alice, the full-duplex Bob transmits the jamming signal to confuse Willie and also receives the signal from Alice simultaneously. To explore the fundamental covertness in such a system, we first provide theoretical modelings for satellite-terrestrial downlink, and the detection error probability of Willie. Based on these models, we then study the transmit power optimization for covert rate maximization. Finally, we present extensive numerical results to validate our theoretical analysis and to illustrate the impact of various system parameters on the maximum covert rate.

articleTitle: Impact of Network Dynamics on Decentralized Federated Learning in LEO Satellite Computing
abstract: The rapid development of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites is transforming satellite computing, creating new opportunities and challenges for global communication and data processing. While LEO satellites offer seamless communication coverage and low latency, their high velocity and limited transmission bandwidth make centralized data processing impractical. Federated Learning (FL) distributes learning across nodes but relies on central ground servers, posing risks of single point failures and extensive communication burdens. Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) emerges as a promising alternative, eliminating the need for central servers by enabling direct model exchanges between neighboring satellites. This approach enhances robustness and scalability by reducing single-point failures and avoiding the need for a known global network topology. However, it should be noted that the performance of DFL is greatly affected by the network topology. This study offers the first investigation into the impact of dynamic network topologies on DFL from the perspective of graph centrality. Specifically, it is observed that an increased satellites communication range can enhance connectivity between nodes and improve the performance of DFL. However, no noticeable relationship is observed between the LEO speed and the connectivity between nodes, nor in the performance of DFL.
